name: Dive Deep
definition: We challenge the data and strive to understand how things really work. We're hands-on and never shy away from getting into the details.

rows.situation: When a number arrives in a deck
rows.under: Repeats it. Has never seen how it was built.
rows.justRight: Asks what it counts, what it excludes, and over what period, before using it.
rows.over: Interrogates every figure until nobody wants to bring you data at all.

rows.situation: When you are told how the process works
rows.under: Takes the description as the reality.
rows.justRight: Goes and watches it run once. The description and the reality are rarely the same.
rows.over: Insists on seeing everything personally, and becomes the constraint on every decision.

rows.situation: When the result is surprisingly good
rows.justRight: Treats a surprise as a sign that something is misunderstood or miscounted, and checks.
rows.over: Assumes every good result is an error, and the team stops reporting wins.

rows.situation: When the detail belongs to the operation
rows.under: Stays at the strategy level, and never sees a shift, a courier, or a kitchen.
rows.justRight: Spends time in the operation often enough that you can smell when a number is wrong.
rows.over: Spends so long in the operation that the strategic work stops happening.

rows.situation: When someone else owns the detail
rows.justRight: Knows enough of the detail to ask the questions that matter, then trusts the owner.
rows.over: Checks every line, and the owner becomes an assistant.

rows.situation: When the same issue keeps coming back
rows.under: Applies the same fix each time.
rows.justRight: Keeps asking why until you reach something that can actually be changed, then changes it.
rows.over: Halts the operation for an investigation into an issue that costs less than the investigation.
